### Added
- `components.<name>.semverFilter` and `gitops.self.semverFilter` select a dev channel: a Go regexp rendered as `OCIRepository.spec.ref.semverFilter`, which Flux applies to the registry's tags before it evaluates the semver range. With a prerelease-admitting range (`>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0-0`) and the filter of one branch's dev builds (`.*-dev\.<sanitized-branch>\..*`) a component — or, under self-management, the chart itself — follows that branch's newest build and never falls back to a stable tag. Unset by default. The dead `components.<name>.filterTags` block (an ImagePolicy field, never an OCIRepository one, undeclared in the schema) is gone.
### Changed
- **BREAKING — meta chart 4.0: `components.kagent` delivers the kagent line (kagent API v2, `kagent.dev/v1alpha3`).** `components.kagent` and the new roster entry `components.kagent-crds` resolve the charts `kagent` and `kagent-crds` of [giantswarm/kagent-upstream](https://github.com/giantswarm/kagent-upstream) (upstream kagent `main` at a pinned commit plus the carried patches) from `oci://ghcr.io/giantswarm/kagent/helm` on the line's release range `>=0.11.0-gs.1 <0.11.1-0` — the releases `0.11.0-gs.N` of upstream 0.11.0, not the line's `0.11.0-dev.giantswarm.…` builds (Flux's Masterminds semver compares prerelease identifiers left to right, `dev` < `gs`; the `-0` on the ceiling admits prereleases at all, and the ceiling holds the patch because a prerelease is confined to no patch tuple; a bare `0.11.0` would be admitted, should upstream's release ever appear at this OCI path) — instead of the `giantswarm/kagent` 0.x wrapper (kagent 0.10, `v1alpha2`) from gsoci. `kagent-crds` renders the five v1alpha3 CRDs as templates carrying `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` (no `crds/` dir, no `crds:` policy), follows `components.kagent` unless switched explicitly (`agent-platform.componentEnabled`), the kagent release and the connectivity release `dependsOn` it, and the render refuses kagent on without it (`agent-platform.validateKagentCrds`). The `kagent:` block names **one build of the line**: `registry: ghcr.io`, the fork's image names (`giantswarm/kagent/{controller,golang-adk,ui}`), an explicit `tag` equal to the chart version of the build (upstream's chart falls back to `.Chart.Version`, which under helm-controller is `<version>+<oci digest>`, an invalid image tag), **`kagent.harness.image`** — the Go ADK image by digest the connectivity chart renders the platform `Harness` from (the CRD accepts no tag) — `controller.substrate.*` (`ate-api`, `atenet-router` in `ate-system`, the default WorkerPool) and `substrateWorkerPool` (`kagent-default`, four gVisor workers on the Giant Swarm Substrate line's worker image), pgvector on the bundled Postgres; a re-pin of the line moves the tag, the digest and the two ranges together from the fork's `builds.md` ledger (README "Re-pinning the kagent line"). Every sibling range selects the kagent API v2 line: `agent-platform-connectivity` `>=4.0.0 <5.0.0` (its own major; the 3.x line held `<4.0.0`), `agent-manager` and `backstage` `1.x` (their 1.0 releases; until published the ranges resolve nothing — both are off by default), `model-manager` `>=0.20.0 <1.0.0` (0.20.0 renders the ModelConfig version the cluster serves; the line stays 0.x); no `semverFilter` anywhere by default, `gitops.self.semverFilter` empty. `agent-manager.agentChart.semver` defaults to `1.x` (was `x.x.x`, which would have rolled the Generic agent chart 1.0.0 to every existing agent the moment it is published). `examples/customer-bom.yaml` pins the line (`kagent` and `kagent-crds` `0.11.0-gs.1` — the same release, one build — `agent-platform-connectivity` `4.0.0`, `agent-manager` and `backstage` `1.0.0`, `model-manager` `0.20.0`). **Every installation acts** ([UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/giantswarm/agent-platform/blob/main/UPGRADE.md) "3.x → 4.0"): the release is inert until the fleet's `agent-platform` range bound (`<4.0.0`) is lifted per installation; a 4.0 installation with kagent on needs Kubernetes 1.35 with the `ClusterTrustBundle`, `ClusterTrustBundleProjection` and `PodCertificateRequest` feature gates and Agent Substrate in `ate-system`. `make verify-meta` (`tests/verify-kagent-wiring.py`, with `tests/fluxsemver.py` reimplementing Flux's constraint semantics offline) asserts the sources, the range's admitted and refused shapes, one build (tag and range on one upstream version, the Harness image a digest), the omitted keys and the retired ones; `make verify-components` the sibling ranges, kagent-crds following kagent and the BOM; `make verify-components-charts` pulls the managers' and the kagent line's charts at what the ranges resolve to (the way Flux resolves, `-gs.N` prereleases included) and renders the forwarded blocks against them — while a range waits for an unpublished release (a sibling's 1.0, the line's first tag) it renders against the build `kagent.tag` names or the newest 0.x and says so.
### Removed
- **The ten bundled example agents' value blocks** (`kagent.k8s-agent` … `kagent.cilium-debug-agent`, each `enabled: false` with `namespaceOverride: kagent`), `kagent.controller.skillsInitImage` and the `METRICS_BIND_ADDRESS` / `METRICS_SECURE` entries of `kagent.controller.env`: the kagent line ships none of the agents and no skills-init image, and its controller serves no Prometheus `/metrics`. With that `kagent.serviceMonitor.enabled` defaults to `false` in both charts and the forwarded `kagent.controller.metrics.enabled` is `false` explicitly — the connectivity chart's controller metrics `Service` and `ServiceMonitor` and upstream's metrics Service would point at a port nothing listens on and sit at `up=0`; nothing reads those metrics (the fleet's `KagentControllerDown` reads kube-state-metrics). `make verify-global` asserts the default renders no kagent monitor and that `kagent.serviceMonitor.enabled: true` still renders it under the global gate; both go back on when upstream serves metrics. The ATS kind smoke keeps kagent and agent-manager off and skips the agent round trips with the reason while the cluster has neither the feature gates nor Substrate (`tests/ats/values-kagent.yaml`, `KAGENT_ON`); agentlab proves them, giantswarm/agent-platform#343 turns them back on.
